name: Cornelia Fermüller
title: Research Scientist; professional-track faculty and PRG co-lead
department: University of Maryland Institute for Advanced Computer Studies; Perception and Robotics Group
fitReason: Strong match for learning robot manipulation from human demonstrations, including force-aware flow-matching policies and active perception. She co-leads Maryland’s Perception and Robotics Group and currently co-advises the first author of ForceBand.

physicalEvidence.summary: June 2026 ForceBand trains a flow-matching policy from human video and wrist sEMG-derived forces, then executes pick–squeeze–place behavior on an actual UR5. The nine-object protocol uses 15 human demonstrations per object and ten evaluation trials. Fermüller is a Maryland coauthor; the project includes Amazon FAR and Johns Hopkins, and hardware location is not settled. Robot deployment uses four Paxini fingertip sensors; a 5 N pre-grasp pause precedes PD tracking of learned force targets.

shortVisit.summary: PRG’s current recruiting page directs prospective degree students to UMD admissions and explicitly scopes listed PhD/master’s/undergraduate projects to admitted students. It gives contact instructions for Fermüller and Aloimonos but no external summer invitation. Current doctoral co-advising is verified independently.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct learned manipulation and force-rich human-to-robot transfer, alongside active robot vision.
scoreReasons.physical: Actual UR5 learned execution with a current advisee, but multi-institution apparatus location/access unresolved.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Admitted-student opportunities and doctoral advising do not establish an outside-master’s invitation.
scoreReasons.freshness: Full June 2026 physical study and current university directory/advisee evidence.

ForceBand’s force-estimation dataset is distinct from its physical policy experiments. Per-user calibration still needs fingertip force sensors; it is not wholly sensor-free. Its squeeze evaluation includes human assessment rather than a universal quantitative force-accuracy criterion.

name: Kun Zhang
school: Carnegie Mellon University; concurrent visiting appointment at MBZUAI
title: Professor at CMU; Visiting Professor of Machine Learning at MBZUAI
department: Department of Philosophy; Machine Learning Department affiliate
fitReason: Useful causal/world-model research match through recent physically evaluated VLA simulation-to-real work. His broader agenda is causal discovery and transferable representations rather than an established independent US manipulation lab.

physicalEvidence.summary: The 2026 Mirage2Matter paper uses reconstructed Gaussian scenes to generate training data for PoSA-VLA, then evaluates the learned policies on a physical AlphaBot 1s with a seven-DoF arm. Actual tasks cover grasping, button pressing and planar pushing/pulling, with 30 trials per task/object. Zhang is a coauthor in a multi-country collaboration; the apparatus is not verified at CMU.

shortVisit.summary: No external-master’s short-visit invitation was found on the inspected personal or university pages. CMU’s Philosophy Graduate Research Visitors page explicitly targets relevant PhD researchers for a few weeks or a term; that departmental invitation is not evidence of master’s eligibility.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct embodied world-model/VLA coauthorship within a broad causal-learning program.
scoreReasons.physical: Actual physical VLA transfer but multi-country collaboration without verified CMU apparatus.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: No master’s short-visit offer; departmental visitor invitation is PhD-scoped.
scoreReasons.freshness: Full 2026 physical preprint and current dual-affiliation official pages.
